text:
marta: Heads up — saw a small but consistent billing spike for a customer after a rolling router rollout. looks like streaming sessions resumed on fallback and we double-counted ~6-10 tokens per event. attaching logs.
aj: can you paste the raw lines? curious if it's retry vs truncated toolcall
marta: sure. excerpt:
```
2026-03-21T14:03:12Z INFO router: session=abc123 route=region-eu -> region-us fallback
2026-03-21T14:03:12Z INFO stream: seq_start=0 seq_end=42 truncated=true toolcall_id=tc-77
2026-03-21T14:03:12Z INFO billing: provisional_tokens=42 session_tag=abc123
2026-03-21T14:03:12Z WARN stream: reconnect attempt=1 resume_token=tkn-9 suffix_loss=true
2026-03-21T14:03:12Z INFO billing: confirmed_tokens=48 session_tag=abc123
```
marta: interesting bit is provisional vs confirmed mismatch — +6 tokens after resume.
sam: hmm toolcall truncation + resume suffix could explain it. router changed affinity in the rollout so resume hit a different backend which accepted the trailing suffix as new output instead of attach.
kevin: do we have a deterministic way to tag resumed fragments as "attached" vs "new" for billing? current ledger key is session_id + seq_start, maybe too coarse.
nora: the console shows a tiny spike for that org at 14:03. viz is noisy but the new provisional->confirmed pipeline seems not surfaceable per-route. we should add a per-route provisional/confirm delta in the dashboard as a short-term signal.
aj: agreed. also need better telemetry: add resume_origin (same-host|fallback) and toolcall_trunc_flag to billing traces.
marta: can someone triage the router behavior — why did affinity flip during rollout? I saw a canary rule change at 14:02:58 from deploy-bot.
deploy-bot: Rolling update started: router-canary v2 -> v3 @ 2026-03-21T14:02:58Z by kevin
kevin: that was the canary to change throttling heuristics. unexpected affinity flip could be due to `max_inflight` threshold change. i can look but will need a reproducer.
aj: for reproducer: simulate a client that streams, triggers a toolcall mid-stream, then triggers a small timeout causing reconnect -> route fallback. That sequence seems to be where we lose suffix ownership.
sam: idea: ledger entry should include resume_id and a fragment_sequence_id; on resume we can dedupe by resume_id+fragment_seq and treat confirmed_tokens as delta over provisional for that fragment only.
nora: UX note: when this happens operators are looking at "tokens per minute" and getting false positives. adding a tiny stateful delta column in the console with a link to raw traces will reduce paging noise.
marta: is there a quick mitigation? maybe treat confirmed_tokens < provisional_tokens + slack_threshold as no-op until we've seen a stability window (eg 5s)?
kevin: that could hide real token refunds though. risky.
aj: short-term safe fix: when resume_origin==fallback && truncated==true && toolcall_id present -> mark confirmed as provisional-anchored (don't create a new consumption record, just reconcile to prior provisional). implement in billing shim.
kevin: ok patch sketch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/routing/pull/842 (WIP) updates router to include resume_origin header and keep session affinity hint for 30s post-fallback.
sam: i'll own billing shim change. will add two new telemetry fields: resume_origin and fragment_seq. will emit a reconcile event `billing.reconcile_hint: true` for the flagged cases.
nora: i'll add a dashboard tile and an alert rule: if per-route provisional->confirmed delta > 0.2% of tokens AND triggered by route-fallback, create a debug-only alert (no on-call) to capture repro data.
marta: thanks. timeline? we should aim for a small mitigation in next 48h.
kevin: i'll finish router header in the canary by EOD.
sam: billing shim PR in review, will request urgent review from @aj.
aj: will review asap. also add tests for fragment_seq idempotency.
billing-bot: NOTE: manual adjustments possible once reconciled. Use /billing-adjust with evidence link.
marta: cool. if anyone sees similar anomalies in other orgs, please ping me and drop logs.
kevin: one more — long-term we should standardize resume semantics across hosted/dedicated/private; will open an RFC after triage.
marta: thanks all :thumbsup
